That depends a lot on what you want out of an RPG. Are you fond of retro RPGs with plenty of difficulty, relatively thin stories with somewhat cliche fantasy elements and random battles? Final Fantasy I-III are for you.

Is story really important to you? Do you like games with a good sense of humor, a nice variety of characters with plenty of personality and strong worldbuilding? Does a world that combines sci-fi and fantasy sound fun to you? If so, Final Fantasy VI will be your jam. It's regarded as one of the best in the series.

Are you looking for a particularly long RPG with a lot of little side stories, some melodrama and minigames? Final Fantasy VII and VIII may suit you, VIII being the angstier of the two.

If you're looking for a game that does a good job refining a lot of the elements that have made Final Fantasy great over the years- characters, humor, worldbuilding, weird villains and a more straightforward fantasy world, check out Final Fantasy IX, which takes the series back to its roots, but with a lot of polish.

Feel like going back to angst? Final Fantasy X. It's a love story that involves time travel, underwater rugby and possibly the most recognizable song in any Final Fantasy game.

I would avoid Final Fantasy 7 at first. It's an absolutely incredible game, but the graphics have aged absolutely horrifically. It was right in that transitional phase between 2D to 3D and so ended up terrible in both regards, relative to modern expectations. Already being familiar with this can easily help you overcome it, but I think it could be hard to get into coming from modern graphics.

Because of this I'd recommend Final Fantasy 6, (3 in the United States). You'd need to get an SNES emulator for it, but the game itself is phenomenal and rivals FF7 on its own merit. The graphical styling also aged a whole lot better than FF7.

For classic FF RPG style I liked FF3 - Three airships, two world maps, job-based character class system. I played the original Famicon ROM and the remake on Steam. Good 50-75 hours of game play.

I also liked 10, and I've been replaying it on Steam lately. Pros: decent story, graphics still look pretty good for ten year old game. Cons: game is rather linear until the end, when you get the airship - even then it's mostly about the mini games, so you get the celestial weapons. Then there is Blitzball - you either love it or you hate it (seems to be my experience).

edit I don't consider it to be a true Final Fantasy game, but it's own thing, Final Fantasy Tactics. Still Tatics is great game if you want a combat tatics game using FF characters, terms, jobs, setting, etc. I do recommend Tactics, but again, I don't think it's a true FF game.
